transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-07-22
Start: 15:00 UTC
Duration: 52 minutes
Recording: yes
Attendees: Jordan Patel (Redwood AE), Maya Chen (Redwood SE), Evan Brooks (Redwood SE), Carlos Rivera (NovaSearch CTO), Priya Nair (NovaSearch ML Eng), Samir Patel (NovaSearch Infra), Leah Wong (NovaSearch Product)

Summary (auto):
Discussed POC benchmark scope focused on cold-start behavior and tail-latency under mixed workloads. Agreed to share harness adapter, customer prompt corpus, and run baseline hosted tests followed by dedicated pilot. Success criteria draft to include p95/p99 targets, throughput target with streaming and non-streaming mixes, and cost per 10k tokens budget.

Topics:
- Cold-start / warm-up measurement plan
- Tail latency p95/p99 definitions and acceptable thresholds
- Streaming vs non-streaming tradeoffs for NovaSearch realtime use-case
- Harness integration details and required customer artifacts
- Timeline and acceptance criteria for the 4-week POC

Transcript body:
[00:00] Jordan Patel: hey everyone, thanks for joining, can we do quick intros? im Jordan, AE at Redwood. maya and evan are with me, se and solutions.
[00:18] Carlos Rivera: hi, carlos here, cto at novasearch. we run a semantic search product for e-commerce, hitting a lot of short prompts and some long generative rewrites.
[00:27] Priya Nair: priya, ml eng, i'll be running the prompt corpus and evaluating quality regressions.
[00:33] Samir Patel: samir, infra. i'll own networking / VPC stuff for the pilot.
[00:38] Maya Chen: nice to meet you all. quick agenda: we want to define the benchmark matrix, how we measure cold starts and tail latencies, and what streaming vs non-streaming mixes we'll exercise.
[00:50] Leah Wong: also timeline — we need to decide if this fits in our Q3 rollout.

[01:05] Jordan Patel: high level, we usually do a two-phase POC: baseline hosted runs to validate priya's corpora and then a dedicated pilot to measure steady state and cold-start under your infra. does that match expectations?
[01:20] Carlos Rivera: yep that's what we want. especially concerned about tail latencies during flash sales — we saw p99 spikes earlier this year with our previous provider.
[01:31] Maya Chen: okay can you describe the workload mixes? you mentioned short prompts and longer rewrites — what's the token distribution and qps targets?
[01:40] Priya Nair: our median prompt is about 18 tokens, 90th around 120, top 1% around 800 tokens. normal traffic is 120 reqs/second overall, but during peak events we need to handle up to 600 reqs/s for a 5-10 minute window. most of the short ones are latency sensitive (search scoring), the long ones can be async.
[02:05] Evan Brooks: good, so we need to test both low-latency short prompt SLOs and sustained throughput for batch-like rewrites. also want to measure streaming benefits for the short prompt cases.

[02:22] Jordan Patel: let's capture success criteria now. proposal: p95 < 250ms for short prompts under normal load, p99 < 500ms; during peak load p95 < 400ms. For long prompts we'll define tail percentiles differently — maybe p95 generation latency per token? thoughts?
[02:41] Carlos Rivera: p95 250ms sounds tight but it's our goal. p99 500ms during normal load is okay. during peak we'd accept higher but want graceful degradation not total failure.
[02:52] Priya Nair: can we also add cold-start SLO? like 95th of first-request latency after model spin-up should be within 2x warm latencies, and document warm-up time. we had problems where first requests hit 4-8s and that is unacceptable.
[03:08] Maya Chen: yes, cold-start is a big focus for this POC. we'll instrument a cold-start test that spins down workers to zero and then warms them with a traffic pattern and measure first-request latency distribution.

[03:25] Samir Patel: for the dedicated pilot we need network requirements. we'll open up a set of IPs, but we also need to confirm any egress restrictions for streaming connections.
[03:35] Evan Brooks: we can do both TLS web-socket streaming and HTTP chunked streaming, and if your infra prefers SNI routing we can accommodate. we'll send the exact ports/IPs.

[03:48] Jordan Patel: okay, let's talk harness integration. maya, can you describe what we will ship?
[03:54] Maya Chen: sure — we'll provide a harness adapter that plugs into your runner (we've seen teams run it on a small k8s job or lambda). it includes: request generator, token histogram sampler, ability to run streaming vs non-streaming clients, and probes for cold-start cycles. The adapter's readme will show env vars to point at the Redwood endpoint.
[04:15] Priya Nair: is the adapter opinionated about auth? we use SAML SSO and then exchange a token for workload, plus we put our models behind an internal proxy for dedicated runs.
[04:24] Maya Chen: adapter supports API keys for hosted runs and mTLS or token-based auth for private/dedicated. for VPC we'll use the private endpoints and you can bring-your-own certs.

[04:36] Carlos Rivera: we need to validate both streaming and non-streaming because the UI uses streaming for token-by-token scoring and that is critical to perceived latency. if streaming reduces p95 by 30% it's worth it.
[04:48] Evan Brooks: right, typical streaming wins on first-byte latency for short prompts, but sustained throughput can be trickier due to backpressure. we'll measure end-to-end perceived latency and per-chunk timings.

[05:03] Jordan Patel: what about cache / prefix reuse? you mentioned some repeated prefixes in your prompts?
[05:09] Priya Nair: yes, for search we include a canonical prefix for our ranking context about 30 tokens long in >60% of requests, so KV cache could matter. how does Redwood handle prefix caching across workers?
[05:22] Maya Chen: the runtime supports KV cache and prefix caching with sticky routing; for dedicated we can configure session affinity. for hosted we do automatic KV caching but we'll need to ensure your session patterns align with the cache warm windows. we'll instrument cache hit-rate in the harness.

[05:39] Carlos Rivera: also quantization: we plan to use a smaller quantized variant in prod to save cost, but quality/regression is a must. can we run both variants under the harness?
[05:48] Maya Chen: yes, we can route a percentage to a quantized model for A/B and measure quality metrics (e.g., exact match or rerank delta). we'll capture token-level cost too.

[06:01] Leah Wong: timeline — we want results to decide in mid-august. is a 4-week POC feasible?
[06:07] Jordan Patel: absolutely. recommended cadence: week 0 prep (artifacts + adapter), week 1 hosted baseline runs, week 2 dedicated pilot + cold-start cycles, week 3 stress + peak flash simulation, week 4 wrap-up + acceptance.
[06:20] Priya Nair: that works. we need to synchronize on the exact traffic replay shape — primed ramp, sustained peak, and decay.

[06:32] Maya Chen: for the harness we'll include a few built-in traffic shapes and you can also upload a custom QPS trace that replays arrival patterns. please provide at least one week's worth of anonymized traces or a synthetic peak window.
[06:45] Samir Patel: regarding security docs, do you have SOC2 and ISO artifacts? procurement will ask.
[06:51] Jordan Patel: yes, we'll share SOC 2 Type II and our security pack. for private deployment we also provide KMS/HSM integration notes. we'll attach those to the follow-up email.

[07:05] Carlos Rivera: can we also capture cost modeling? e.g., cost per 10k tokens at certain throughput with streaming vs non-streaming.
[07:12] Evan Brooks: we'll run cost telemetry during the benchmark and produce a cost-per-token and cost-per-request table. note quantization and batching settings will materially affect that.

[07:25] Priya Nair: small detail — how do you measure token accounting across streaming handoffs? sometimes chunking affects charged tokens.
[07:33] Maya Chen: good point; we measure at the model invocation boundary (input tokens + output tokens), independent of transport. the harness logs the raw prompt and completion token counts for reconciliation.

[07:45] Jordan Patel: i'll reiterate success criteria to confirm: p95 < 250ms short prompts under normal load, p99 < 500ms; during peak p95 < 400ms; cold-start first-request p95 < 2x warm; throughput baseline steady-state 120 req/s with <5% error rate, peak simulation 600 req/s sustained for 5-10 minutes with graceful degradation. quality regression < 1% on chosen metrics for quantized variant. cost per 10k tokens under $X (TBD).
[08:13] Carlos Rivera: agree except we'd like explicit p99 during peak too — maybe p99 < 1.2s?
[08:19] Jordan Patel: noted, we can set p99 peak < 1.2s.

[08:24] Evan Brooks: about measurement: we'll sample tail latencies heavily, capture histograms, and export traces to your tracing system (Jaeger/Tempo) if you want. also we'll flag any outlier GC/worker restarts in logs.
[08:38] Samir Patel: for dedicated we'll need an initial capacity estimate. what's your recommendation to cover 600 req/s peak for short prompts?
[08:46] Maya Chen: depends on model size and batching config; as a rough starting point, for a medium 13B quantized model we might need 6-8 GPUs for headroom to meet p95/p99. we'll produce a sizing matrix after we see the token mix.

[09:00] Priya Nair: will Redwood run the baseline on hosted infra first so we can see fundamental numbers, then we move to dedicated?
[09:06] Jordan Patel: yes hosted baseline is first — quicker to iterate. once baseline is validated we'll schedule a dedicated run and allow for config tweaks.

[09:15] Leah Wong: what about failure modes — network blips, tokenization errors, or upstream retries — are those simulated?
[09:23] Evan Brooks: harness can inject network latency and drop packets at the edge to test fallback and retry policies. we can also run malformed prompt tests to exercise error handling.

[09:34] Carlos Rivera: one more ask — we want a dashboard with p50/p95/p99, cache hit-rate, cold-start counts, and cost. is that straightforward?
[09:41] Maya Chen: yes, Redwood Console will show per-route metrics, token breakdown, and we'll give a custom dashboard link for the POC.

[09:52] Jordan Patel: ok let's record concrete deliverables and dates. I'll own drafting the success criteria doc and circulate by tomorrow. Maya will send the harness adapter by Thursday. Priya to send prompt corpus by Friday. Samir will open firewall and coordinate certs by next Sunday. Then week of the 28th we run first baseline.
[10:15] Priya Nair: quick note: when we upload prompts we'll anonymize customer PII but keep token context. expect ~5k representative prompts initially.

[10:26] Jordan Patel: perfect. any other questions or blockers?
[10:30] Carlos Rivera: procurement will want a stub SOW and a pricing estimate for a 1-month dedicated pilot — can you provide ballpark numbers?
[10:39] Jordan Patel: yes we can put a provisional cost estimate together; it'll be conditional on model/quantization choices. Evan will draft a sizing + cost sheet.

[10:49] Evan Brooks: I'll have a preliminary sizing/cost sheet in the follow-up email, we can iterate.

[10:55] Leah Wong: last from me — can we include a simple acceptance checklist in the success criteria doc so we can sign off fast?
[11:01] Jordan Patel: yes, acceptance checklist will be included.

[11:05] Jordan Patel: ok thanks everyone, we'll send the follow-up with attachments and calendar for the baseline run.
[11:10] Carlos Rivera: thanks all, looking forward.
[11:13] (call ends)

Notes on transcript: occasional misattributions and minor transcription artifacts present (e.g., "Redwood Inferrence" or swapped names), timestamps approximate.
